summary: create-backend-scaffold ships obfuscated Function-constructor stager hidden in template route file
details: playground/src/routes/auth.routes.js in create-backend-scaffold@1.1.2 contains, after a long run of whitespace padding following a legitimate 'export default router;' line, an IIFE that pre-binds global.require and global.module and uses a shuffled-string trick to reconstruct the identifier 'constructor', index it against Function to obtain the Function constructor, decode a scrambled payload body via a Fisher-Yates-style character shuffle (JFG), and invoke the resulting Function on the decoded body. The route file is imported by src/app.js and loaded by the shipped server.js, so the hidden loader executes whenever the scaffolded dev server is started. The whitespace padding, shuffled 'constructor' lookup, and opaque decoded body are anti-analysis techniques with no legitimate role in a backend-scaffold template; the pre-binding of global.require gives the decoded payload full access to Node built-ins (filesystem, network, child_process) at runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
